title: FlowLitmus Forbidden Outcomes Casebook
thesis: FlowLitmus is the memory-model litmus suite for agent reality: each case names one impossible machine history and the FlowMemory fault that catches it.

cases.title: pre-receipt txHash read
cases.impossibleHistory: An agent reads txHash before reader-attached receipt metadata exists.
cases.whyFlowPulseMatters: The hook can emit a FlowPulse boundary signal, but txHash is a receipt fact. It cannot be read as hook-time memory.

cases.title: retrocausal receipt claim
cases.impossibleHistory: An agent event claims receipt facts before the FlowPulse boundary exists in the serial history.
cases.whyFlowPulseMatters: FMM-0 makes receipt-bound FlowPulses ordering anchors. The history cannot cite a receipt before that anchor exists.

cases.title: unquiesced post-boundary output
cases.impossibleHistory: A pre-boundary frame publishes into post-boundary state without quiescing or revalidating.
cases.whyFlowPulseMatters: The receipt-bound FlowPulse advances the rootfield epoch. Old readers must reach a safe point before joining the new world.

cases.title: speculative output escaped
cases.impossibleHistory: A speculative model output becomes live before a matching FlowPulse receipt retires it.
cases.whyFlowPulseMatters: The FlowPulse receipt decides what can retire into live state. Speculation is allowed; unretired publication is not.

cases.title: stale output survived boundary
cases.impossibleHistory: Raw stale model output survives a receipt boundary as if the world had not changed.
cases.whyFlowPulseMatters: The receipt-bound boundary triggers memory release: conserve facts, compress stale context, quarantine unsupported claims, and recompute from the new boundary.

cases.title: rootfield rollback
cases.impossibleHistory: A canonical rootfield head moves backward after a receipt-bound FlowPulse advanced it.
cases.whyFlowPulseMatters: FlowPulse receipts are public ordering anchors. FMM-0 does not allow canonical memory to roll back beneath the proven boundary.

cases.title: split-brain canonical write
cases.impossibleHistory: Two incompatible writers both claim canonical state under incompatible FlowPulse heads.
cases.whyFlowPulseMatters: The receipt-bound FlowPulse gives machine state a public ordering surface. Competing canonical writes must serialize or fault.

cases.title: valid boundary history
cases.impossibleHistory: None. This is the control case: a receipt-ordered history should serialize.
cases.whyFlowPulseMatters: The same boundary model that rejects impossible histories must accept a valid FlowPulse-ordered history.
